title: Cabarets where father played; pianists Kokai George and Udell Wilson
summary: Father played at Tom Anderson's on Basin Street and a Liberty Street cabaret; Arthur recalls pianists Kokai George and Udell Wilson.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Do you remember any of the cabarets that you went to to see your father play? Do you remember any that he played at?
I'll tell you where he played. You know we had a cabaret at the time? He used to play in Tom Anderson.
You know what at that place? Yeah, was that the one on Rambord Street? Or did he have a couple places?
He had one on Basin Street and one on Rambord Street. He had one on Basin Street and one on Rambord Street. He used to play. Tom Anderson on Basin Street. I remember that cabaret.
In the corner of there of the Custom House in the Basin. Yeah.

Somewhere around where Lula White's house was at. He played around there. And that was Tom Anderson. I remember hearing him saying he played at Tom Anderson when I was at Kidney Shopping. He spoke of the place where he played. I remember that place. Let's see. We had another cabaret on Liberty Street. He played in there but I can't remember the name of that place. I can't remember the name of that cabaret. In fact, I was such a young kid. I wasn't interested in there. I didn't pay much attention to those things in them days. But Tom Anderson, he played there so long and so often that I remember hearing him speak of that place, you know, around the shop, he'd speak about the place. Now they had another fellow probably you never heard talk of. You ever heard him speak of, Kokai George?
Wait a minute, I'm not sure. No.
That was a good piano player.
Kokai? Kokai George. He was cross-iron. They used to call him Kokai George, you know. He was a great piano player too. Around there.
And then they had another boy, I guess you heard speak of him. I don't believe he was from here, but he played a lot of piano in the district and during them times. Udel.
Oh yeah, Udel Wilson. Was that the name of him?
Yeah, Udel Wilson. I remember him. He came from Kansas City. Yeah, he was a tall, brown skin boy. I knew him well.
A few people told us about him.

Yeah, well I had grown up when he was playing, that's why I knew him well, you see. He played on, right there on Franklin Street. They used to have a cabaret on Franklin. He used to play in that cabaret at night.
I remember him. The entertainers, do you remember that? I remember the entertainers. The tuxedo was on there too. You were pretty young. The villa, it was the villa by the time you came up.
Maybe the turf, I think it later changed to the turf.

I don't remember them so well. I remember the entertainers and Tom Anderson, I remember those places. But like you said, they had two, I don't know anything about the one on Rambo. I remember the one on Basin Street. I remember they had one around there, he played around there.
